key_insight: Raising cold-spray pressure from 30 to 60 bar increases copper particle velocity past the bonding threshold, producing denser deposits with better conductivity and ductility through stronger inter-particle bonding and recrystallization.
engineering_relevance: For CSAM copper parts, spray pressure is a key control knob that can balance electrical performance, tensile ductility, and strength without melting the feedstock.
method: LightSPEE3D cold spray of copper at 30, 40, 50, and 60 bar
Characterization by XRD, SEM, hardness, eddy current conductivity, and tensile testing
Correlation of particle velocity with microstructural evolution and mechanical/electrical properties
evidence_signal: The abstract reports pressure-dependent gains in particle velocity, XRD crystallite refinement, increased conductivity, and a shift toward more ductile tensile and fracture behavior at higher pressures.
watch_item: Higher pressure improved performance but also reduced hardness, so process tuning must avoid over-annealing/recovery effects if surface wear resistance is important.
paper_title: Optimising Cold Spray Additive Manufacturing: Pressure-driven enhancement of mechanical performance in copper deposits
